subject: conditioning sigma in multilevel regression with measurement error

messages.author: 3a2c786220b0276c
messages.subject: conditioning sigma in multilevel regression with measurement error
parts:
I've been trying to condition the variance of a gaussian multilevel regression to a predictor (in the context of a meta-analysis).

This works ok (except for some divergences I'll have to work through):

bf1 <- bf(GaussianOutcome ~ 1 + Condition + (1 + Condition | Study),
              sigma ~ 1 + Condition)

m1 <- brm(bf1,
               data = d, family=gaussian(),iter = 500, warmup = 200, chains=2, cores = 2,
               control= list(adapt_delta = 0.95,max_treedepth=15))



However, I have a measure of uncertainty for the outcome, and I'm a bit at loss as how to implement it. The following fails with "Error: Cannot predict or fix 'sigma' in this model."


bf2 <- bf(GaussianOutcome | se(GaussianOutcome_SE) ~ 1 + Condition + (1 + Condition | Study),
              sigma ~ 1 + Condition)


m2 <- brm(bf2,
               data = d, family=gaussian(),iter = 500, warmup = 200, chains=2, cores = 2,
               control= list(adapt_delta = 0.95,max_treedepth=15))

Any suggestions on how to deal with this?

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] conditioning sigma in multilevel regression with measurement error
parts:
By default, | se(.) will fix sigma to 0. To avoid that, go for | se(GaussianOutcome_SE, sigma = TRUE).

See also ?resp_se
